description.purpose: A telephone as a CHANNEL of a person, with FreeSWITCH as the switch it is named after (it succeeds `phone@1.0.0`, a name that no longer exists: it said the medium where it should have said the machine). FreeSWITCH stays the media edge in gateway mode -- it does the SIP and forks the audio over a WebSocket -- and this hive is both halves of what a colony needs beside it: the MEDIA half is a `voice` cell that carries the sound, the SIGNALLING half is a small state machine that knows who is on the line and turns the facts about the line that a person could answer -- and only those -- into turns of the member's conversation. The two live in one hive because a call is one thing, bound by one id: FreeSWITCH's channel UUID is the `?session=` of the audio fork and therefore the session an answer is spoken back into. Since 2.0.0 the SWITCH is the proxy: which number reaches this member, and what a caller has to type before they are put through, are rows in the switch's own database, written by three tools this hive offers (`add_number`, `set_pin`, `disable_pin`) and read by the dialplan; a `call_incoming` that carries `hop.user_id` is trusted as the identity the switch verified, and `params.callers` is the fallback for a dialplan that stamps none. The media half answers on a MOUNT of the colony's one listener and owns no port (`voice@2.0.0`), which is what makes one dialplan extension enough for every colony a switch serves. First place, because both of those are surfaces somebody wires against.
description.use_when: Wherever a person should be reachable by telephone, or should be able to ring somebody up. Instantiate it in `<member>/channels` under the name `freeswitch` -- the NODE is the machine, `context.channel` stays `phone`, which is the kind of conversation, draw the two channel edges the way a `voice` channel draws them, and point the dialplan's `curl` at the hive's own address. The assistant is offered five tools over the tool v-lanes the member declares at its rim: `call` and `hangup` for a call, and `add_number`, `set_pin` and `disable_pin` for the line. Give `./signal` a `line_user_id` -- the member a caller of this line is put through as -- or the three line tools refuse by name.
description.not_in_scope: It is not a switch and holds no trunk: SIP, codecs, dialplans and voicemail belong to FreeSWITCH and stay there. It authenticates nobody: since 2.0.0 the SWITCH does, and this hive trusts the stamp it puts on an inbound call. It keeps no register of numbers and no PIN at all -- the three line tools WRITE the switch's table and nothing reads it back here -- and a call with neither a stamp nor a `callers` entry is refused, its leg put down so the dialplan has it back. A second call is decided rather than ignored: `params.second_call` is `busy`, `queue` or `parallel` up to `params.capacity`, and every outcome leaves a row in the call table and a receipt on its own lane. And it holds no persona: what is said into a call is a turn of the member's conversation, answered by the member's own assistant. It does not narrate the line either: a ring, an answer that only confirms a call already announced, and the END of a call are booked in the call table and said to nobody (GH #614) -- a model answers everything it is handed, and a farewell into a line that is already down is what that costs.
examples: PORTS - Entry: `in_speak` (the answer to be spoken), and the four dialplan events `call_incoming`, `call_ringing`, `call_answered`, `call_ended`, which reach the front door as `POST /messages` addressed at this hive. Two lanes name a connect point: `tool` and `schemas`, both `to: <freeswitch>/dial`. Exit: `turn`, `partial`, `error`, `tool_result`, `tool_schemas` and, since 1.1.0, the four arbitration receipts `call_accepted`, `call_queued`, `call_refused` and `call_abandoned` -- all at the hive path. The installing manifest draws the edge that drains the receipts, or they dead-letter.

somebody rings the member -> ONE turn 'Incoming call from +49…', carrying the call the audio runs under and the sender id the number maps to; the `call_answered` the dialplan sends a moment later books the state and says nothing
the model calls `call` -> an originate at the switch with `origination_uuid` and an `api_on_answer` that starts `uuid_audio_stream` on `?session=<uuid>`, and a turn the moment somebody picks up

hangup while the assistant is still talking -> the row is marked, the line stays up, and the `speak_end` of that same call is what fires `uuid_kill`; a sentence cut short (`speak_end` with reason `cancelled` or `failed`) fires `uuid_break <uuid> all`, because the half sentence the caller is still hearing sits at the switch and `mod_audio_stream` offers no clear of its own.

the far end hangs up -> the row goes to `ended` with its cause, and nothing is said: the line an answer would be spoken into is gone. If somebody was waiting in the queue, that end of a call is what promotes them: hold media off, audio fork on, one `call_accepted` receipt with cause `dequeued`, and their turn
